newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Police arrest Bangladesh opposition leaders.
newsitem.headline: Police arrest Bangladesh opposition leaders.

text.p: Police in a pre-dawn swoop on Thursday arrested four key leaders of the main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), police and family sources said.
Arrested were former ministers Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain, Abdul Mannan and Goyeswar Roy, and former Mayor of Dhaka Mirza Abbas.
Police also raided the house of former minister Sadek Hossain Khoka but he managed to escape, his family said.

The raid followed BNP's call on Wednesday for a countrywide general strike on Sunday, a working day in mainly Moslem Bangladesh, in an attempt to topple the government of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
"We can't give them any more time. They have proved more than inefficient in running the country," BNP chief and former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia told a party rally in Dhaka.
She urged all nationalist forces to "observe a countrywide strike from dawn to 2 p.m. on March 23 to overthrow the inefficient, corrupt and anti-people government".
"Hundreds of police in uniform and civil dress stormed our house around 5 a.m. and just asked him to follow them," said a relative of Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain, former energy minister.
"They produced no warrants and explained nothing," said a nephew of Abdul Mannan, former textile and civil aviation minister.
Police said they were picked up by detectives but would not say on what charges.
Political analysts were divided on the possible impact of the arrests.
Some said they believed the "hard line" taken by Hasina's government was necessary to ensure political stability. Others said Hasina should have waited for public reaction to BNP's strike call.
Khaleda branded Hasina's government "shamelessly pro-Indian", and said it had conspired to "let the big hegemonist power enhance its influence on the small neighbour".
"We can no longer cooperate with this government or keep silent when national interests are at stake," Khaleda told cheering supporters.
Khaleda also attacked Hasina's handling of the economy.
Hasina took office last June after the Awami League defeated the BNP in general elections billed free and fair at home and abroad.
The strike is the first major challenge faced by the eight-month-old government.
